summary: AN INTERACTIVE 7-PAGE STORY USING CANVA CALLED “ABANDONED, BUT NOT FORGOTTEN” THE STORY EXPLAINS HOW NASA HAVE LEFT PIECES OF THEIR HISTORIC HARDWARE ON THE MOON,MARS AND VENUS SINCE THE 1960S. USING INTERACTIVE CHARACTER DIALOGUE AND FUN SCIENTIFIC FACTS WE CAN EDUCATE SCHOOL AND SPACE LOVERS ABOUT THE HARDWARE AND THE AMAZING SCIENCE IT HAS ENABLED
details:
“ABANDONED, BUT NOT FORGOTTEN” IS AN INTERACTIVE 7-PAGE DIGITAL STORYBOOK AND COSMIC MUSEUM TOUR DESIGNED TO MAKE NASA’S HISTORIC SPACE HARDWARE ENGAGING, EDUCATIONAL, AND ACCESSIBLE FOR SCHOOL-AGE CHILDREN.

THE PROJECT OPERATES THROUGH A CREATIVE NARRATIVE FRAMEWORK WHERE HISTORIC SPACE EXPLORATION RELICS INCLUDING APOLLO LUNAR MODULES AND RETROREFLECTORS, VIKING MARS ROVER, AND VENERA VENUS LANDERS TELL THEIR OWN STORIES DIRECTLY TO THE READER THROUGH CHARACTER DIALOGUE. RATHER THAN PRESENTING A DENSE, STATIC TECHNICAL REPORT, THE PROJECT GAMIFIES LEARNING. EACH STOP ON THE TOUR BLENDS IMMERSIVE STORYTELLING WITH CLEAR SCIENCE FACTS, CONCLUDING WITH AN INTERACTIVE REFLECTION CHALLENGE THAT ENCOURAGES YOUNG LEARNERS TO THINK ABOUT FUTURE SPACE ENGINEERING AND EXPLORATION.

DEVELOPED ENTIRELY USING CANVA, THE PROJECT LEVERAGES INTERACTIVE PAGE-LINKING BUTTONS,RICH GRAPHIC ASSETS, AND STRUCTURED LAYOUTS. IN DESIGNING THE PRESENTATION, I CAREFULLY CONSIDERED SEVERAL CRITICAL FACTORS. FIRST, I TAILORED THE VOCABULARY AND TONE SPECIFICALLY FOR SCHOOL AGED CHILDREN TO ENSURE THE CONTENT REMAINED APPROACHABLE AND UNINTIMIDATING.SECOND, I ADDRESSED VISUAL ACCESSIBILITY BY IMPLEMENTING HIGH-CONTRAST COLOR CHOICES, SUCH AS PURE WHITE AND NEON YELLOW TEXT AGAINST COMPLEX BACKGROUND LIKE RED MARTIAN.THIRD, CONSIDERING THE 7-PAGE SLIDE LIMIT CONSTRAINT WE PACKED COMPREHENSIVE SCIENTIFIC NARRATIVE INTO A CONCISE, WELL-BALANCED FORMAT WITHOUT OVERCROWDING THE VISUAL SPACE.

THE BENEFITS AND IMPACT OF THIS PROJECT ARE PROFOUND . BY TRANSFORMING DISCARDED SPACE RELICS INTO RELATABLE EDUCATIONAL HEROES, IT SPARKS EARLY CURIOSITY IN YOUNG MINDS. MORE IMPORTANTLY, IT CONTEXTUALIZES CONTEMPORARY SPACE SCIENCE, HELPING STUDENTS UNDERSTAND HOW THE ABANDONED HARDWARE LEFT ACROSS THE MOON,MARS, AND VENUS SINCE THE 1960S LAID THE VITAL GROUNDWORK FOR MODERN SPACE EXPLORATION. ULTIMATELY, THIS PROJECT BRIDGES THE GAP BETWEEN HISTORICAL PRESERVATION AND FUTURISTIC CURIOSITY, TURNING FORGOTTEN RELICS INTO TIMELESS INSPIRATIONS FOR THE NEXT GENERATION OF SPACE EXPLORERS
